title: Asymptotic scars arising from the remnants of quantum phase transitions
authors: Leonard Logarić, Shane Dooley, Tsuyoshi Okubo, Nobuyuki Yoshioka
abstract: Many-body localisation, Hilbert space fragmentation and quantum many-body scars (QMBS) are well-established mechanisms of ergodicity breaking in quantum systems. Recently, asymptotic quantum many-body scars (AQMBS), non-thermal states whose stability grows with system size, have been proposed theoretically and probed experimentally. Here, we show that AQMBS arise naturally as remnants of certain quantum phase transitions. For a broad class of frustration-free Hamiltonians, we prove that their gapless excitations survive deformation into a scarred Hamiltonian as states whose energy variance is bounded by the excitation gap. Consequently, the gapless excitations at a quantum critical point become AQMBS of the scarred Hamiltonian. Their fidelity relaxation time is then set by the critical scaling of the gap, determined by the dynamic critical exponent. Modelling the critical Fredkin and Motzkin chains and the two-dimensional PVBS model, we obtain AQMBS whose variances directly reflect the dynamic exponents of the underlying transitions. Where the gap of the Motzkin chain closes super-exponentially, we find exponentially stable AQMBS, for which we also observe numerical evidence of volume-law entanglement.
summary: This paper establishes that Asymptotic Quantum Many-Body Scars (AQMBS) emerge naturally from the gapless excitations found at quantum critical points. The stability of these scars is rigorously shown to be dictated by the rate at which the energy gap closes in the underlying reference Hamiltonian. By modeling systems like the Fredkin and Motzkin chains, the authors provide quantitative evidence linking critical scaling exponents to the long-term dynamics of quantum states.
main_problem: The paper investigates Asymptotic Quantum Many-Body Scars (AQMBS), which are non-thermal states whose stability increases with system size, and proves they arise naturally as remnants of quantum phase transitions.
main_result: The gapless excitations at a quantum critical point of a reference Hamiltonian deform into AQMBS of a scarred Hamiltonian, with the state's stability directly governed by the gap closing rate of the underlying transition.
method: The authors use theoretical proofs (Theorem 1 and 2) to bound the energy variance of the scarred Hamiltonian by the gap of the reference Hamiltonian, supplemented by numerical simulations on specific models.
model_or_system: The study analyzes a broad class of frustration-free Hamiltonians, including the critical Fredkin chain, the Motzkin spin chain, and the two-dimensional Product Vacua with Boundary State (PVBS) model.
key_observables: Fidelity relaxation time ($T_{	ext{rel}}$), energy variance ($\delta^2 \hat{H}_S$), and the energy gap ($\Delta_k(N)$) of the reference Hamiltonian.
important_parameters: The dynamic critical exponent ($z$) governing the gap closing rate ($\Delta(N) \sim N^{-z}$), and the system size $N$.
main_assumptions: The Hamiltonians are assumed to be frustration-free, and the analysis relies on the existence of gapless excitations at the quantum critical point.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the decay of fidelity and magnetization for various models (Fredkin, PVBS), showing how the decay rate scales with system size and how this scaling matches the gap closing rate.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by proving that gapless excitations become AQMBS (Theorem 1 & 2). It then applies this framework to specific models like the Fredkin and Motzkin chains, and the 2D PVBS model, demonstrating the predicted scaling laws.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical link between the critical behavior of quantum phase transitions (gap closing) and the emergence of long-lived, non-thermal quantum states (scars) in the system's dynamics.
